text:
Dylan Larkin isn't playing for the Red Wings, and that is still the story of their season. He wants out and has stopped playing until Detroit trades him, and the Detroit Free Press reported this week that the team has offers but "value is not there." Defenseman Simon Edvinsson is in his own standoff, with Toronto reported among the teams in the mix (Daily Faceoff). Two of the franchise's core pieces are, for now, trade chips.

Without Larkin, Detroit is 8-11-3 with 19 points and 3-7 in its last ten, including Wednesday's loss to Boston in the club's centennial game. The frustrating part is that the play hasn't been that bad. The Wings have 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances); they've scored 12.09 fewer goals than those chances usually produce, and by our count that has cost them about 3.9 points. Alex DeBrincat is the face of it, 3 points in his last 10 against 8.4 expected.

The crease is a two-way split. John Gibson is at .851 and 4.7 goals worse than expected over his last five starts; Daniil Tarasov is at .927 and 3.8 better, even with a 1-4-0 record, and Todd McLellan has kept turning to him. Marco Kasper's role is growing. Our playoff odds are 14%. If the shooting comes back, the hole is climbable. If Larkin and Edvinsson leave, the conversation changes entirely.
headline: Detroit's season is waiting on Larkin
